Risk call: this is a refuse-or-minimum situation, and I'd lean refuse.

Positives: the coin is alive, not an airdrop factory, top-3 holders are only 8%, and the pool holds 142 SOL. Volume is real ($78k in 15 min).

Concerns: bundle share is 38%, meaning a large portion of the curve was bundled buys, and the first two minutes after graduation show sells at 93% of buys with a launch bot present. Last-15-min net flow is only +20.9 SOL on 342 SOL of buying, so sellers are nearly matching buyers. The 26% drawdown from the 30-minute high is already underway.

If the desk insists on buying: $5 ticket, 25% stop, 30-minute max hold. Refuse any size if the pool drops below ~100 SOL, bundle share is confirmed as coordinated wallets, or net flow turns negative.
memos.scout:
Case for buying "Sid" now, at 30 minutes, is thin but not empty. The coin is marked ORGANIC with no airdrop dump seen, and it has 859 curve buyers with a top-3 holder share of only 7.95%, so no single wallet dominates. Over the last 15 minutes it took $78k volume and 981 buyers against 867 sellers, with net SOL flow of +20.9 and a 22% return. It is 26% off its 30-minute high, which is a pullback rather than a collapse, and it is still up 159% over 30 minutes. The pool holds 142 SOL, deep enough that a $20 ticket shouldn't move it much.

The weak points are real. Buyers were nearly as numerous as sellers in the last 15 minutes, the 2-minute post-graduation sell-to-buy ratio was 0.93, and a 38% bundle share suggests some coordinated early buying. Those are signs demand may be fading, not building. My honest read: a modest case exists for a small entry if you believe the pullback is a pause, but the base rates for alive, post-graduation buys are negative and the signals of continued demand are mixed. Skipping is defensible.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is insider distribution into a thin, sell-heavy tape. The bundle share is 38.5%, meaning a large slice of early supply was bought in coordinated bundles, and the launch bot was present in the first two minutes. Early buyers have likely been holding since graduation. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.93 in the first two minutes shows heavy early selling pressure, and last 15 minutes had 320.8 SOL sold against 341.7 bought, with net flow only +20.9 SOL. Sellers (867) nearly match buyers (981), so the tape is distributing, not accumulating. The 26% drawdown from the 30-minute high after a 159% run-up is consistent with that exit. With a 142 SOL pool, a $20 round trip faces 1.4 to 5.1% in fees and impact, so even a modest bounce may not cover costs. Recommend skip.
